optional_codes.reason: Unqualified visual loss, right eye, normal vision left eye: describes the same loss of vision in less specific terms. Against it, Section I.C.7.b assigns a code from H54.6- when blindness or low vision in one eye is documented, and the note documents neither; the left eye is recorded as a normal examination, not as normal vision. Defensible either way.

unsupported_codes.reason: Retinal vascular occlusions, the category that holds central retinal artery occlusion: reporting a code from it treats the diagnosis as established, and the note gives it only as 'compatible with'.

citations.H53.131: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section IV.H: in the outpatient setting a diagnosis documented as 'compatible with', or with another term that indicates uncertainty, is not coded; the condition is coded to the highest degree of certainty for the visit, such as symptoms or signs. Here the assessment is sudden visual loss of the right eye with findings compatible with central retinal artery occlusion, so the visual loss is reported, with the code whose title matches the provider's wording, and the occlusion is not.

coder_notes: The rule holds although the fundus findings are the classic ones and the patient was sent urgently for stroke evaluation: the provider's own wording is 'compatible with'. The retinal findings are exam findings and are not coded on their own. No blindness category is reported: the provider documents neither blindness nor low vision, and no measured acuity. No cerebrovascular diagnosis is made at this visit.
